messages:
sami: Heads-up — we're debating header semantics for tiered routing + fallback. Current SDK sets X-RW-Region, X-RW-Tier, X-RW-Debug. Do we want Tier as an enum ("free|standard|pro|enterprise") or a numeric priority? Also, how should quota enforcement interact with automatic fallback to lower-tier model variants?
ton: numeric priority is simpler for merge logic (higher number = higher preference). enums complicate ordering when a customer has multiple entitlements.
priya: enums are friendlier in console UX and policy rules. You can still map enum -> priority server-side, but the SDK/console should surface human names.
lee: telemetry requirement: we must record routing decision, chosen variant, and fallback reason. console needs per-route breakdown: #requests, fallback rate, avg latency per variant.
eva: important: fallback must not skirt quota. If a request is billed against tier A but falls back to tier B variant, billing & quota attribution need to be explicit. Either bill at original request tier or bill at served-variant tier (and adjust quota). Both have compliance implications.
ops-bot: feature-flag: routing.fallback.strict_quota=false rolled out to canary.
sami: good point on billing. My preference: attribution stays with the original requested tier for accounting, but logs include served_variant for cost calc and anomaly detection. Need product sign-off.
priya: UX: add X-RW-Allow-Fallback: true/false header. Default false for strict customers. Console toggle per-API-key that sets allow_fallback. Also add X-RW-Prefer-Variant to hint specific model family (e.g., "redwood-ggml-1.3-small").
ton: implementation notes: server will evaluate route table by: 1) match exact region, 2) match tier/policy, 3) if no capacity then if Allow-Fallback true -> find compatible variant with next-lowest priority, attach fallback_reason="capacity" or "policy".
lee: telemetry event names: routing.decision, routing.fallback, routing.quota_violation. Include fields: requested_tier, served_variant, fallback_chain, latency_ms, cost_tokens.
eva: edge case: what if fallback variant is in a different region? That could violate data residency. Need to check per-API-key residency flag before allowing cross-region fallback.
sami: yes — add X-RW-Region-Strict: true to opt-out of cross-region fallback. Default is false for hosted.
priya: quick SDK header example to discuss in RFC:
```
X-RW-Region: eu-west-1
X-RW-Tier: enterprise
X-RW-Allow-Fallback: true
X-RW-Region-Strict: false
X-RW-Routing-Debug: sample-token
X-RW-Prefer-Variant: redwood-q4a
```
ton: about X-RW-Routing-Debug: ensure restricted to internal tokens or admin keys; we don't want customers flipping debug in prod. Log level gating + sampling is needed.
lee: console rollout UX: add a per-key "Routing safeguards" card: Allow fallback (on/off), Cross-region fallback (on/off), Preferred variants (whitelist), Telemetry level. Also surface projected cost delta if fallback is allowed (est. percent of requests hitting lower-cost variants).
eva: testing checklist: unit tests for header parsing, integration tests simulating capacity pressure, e2e billing simulation to ensure attribution works, telemetry events validate shape.
priya: API change risk: minimal if we keep headers optional and default to current behavior (no fallback unless customer opts-in). We should document fallback behavior and edge cases in SDK docs.
sami: action items: 1) priya -> draft RFC for header contract + console mapping (due EOD Wed). 2) tony -> prototype server routing logic + unit tests (start Mon). 3) lee -> telemetry schema + console mockups (due Thu). 4) eva -> billing/quotas impact analysis (due Fri).
ops-bot: RFC created: rfc/2026-routing-headers-fallback-draft.md (link) — canary flag is on for internal dev cluster.
sami: cool. one more minor ask — make the routing.fallback telemetry include token-level sample ids so we can correlate with cost spikes without storing PII.
lee: noted. I'll include sample_id and sampling_rate in the schema.
priya: +1. I'll start the docs page and SDK helper to set headers easily.
ton: small nit: consider X-RW-Tier-Priority as alternate header name if we expose numeric priority. keep both? might be confusing. prefer one canonical header set.
sami: agree, canonical set: X-RW-Region, X-RW-Tier (enum), X-RW-Allow-Fallback, X-RW-Region-Strict, X-RW-Prefer-Variant, X-RW-Routing-Debug. Server maps Tier->priority internally.
eva: sounds good. I'll calendar a quick sync with finance after RFC is ready to confirm cost attribution.
priya: thanks all — will post RFC link here when ready.
